minors.title: Delay of game is charged to the offense even when the defense never called a play
minors.description: When the play clock expires in PLAY_CALL, the flag is built with team: offense if EITHER selection is still null. The CPU always sends its call within cpuCallMinTicks (18) + jitter (14) ticks, so the only way this branch fires with a missing defensive call is a human on defense who has not picked. The penalty then moves the CPU offense back 5 yards and replays the down, benefitting the team that actually stalled. Nothing pauses the sim during play selection (App.ts only pauses on the 'pause' screen), so the play clock really does run out on the play-call screen.
minors.failureScenario: User is team 1 (defense). CPU offense has 2nd & 6 at midfield and submits its call at tick+~25. User leaves the play-call screen open until the 40-second play clock hits 0. enforceDeadBallFoul fires with team = offense: the CPU is flagged for delay of game, loses 5 yards, and replays 2nd down. Repeatable every play, half-the-distance all the way back.

minors.title: Interception fumbled back to the passing team does not reset the down series
minors.description: resolveLooseBall sets o.changeOfPossession = pl.team !== e.playOffense (src/sim/phases/playLive.ts:544), so when the passing team recovers a fumble by the interceptor, changeOfPossession goes back to false. applySeries then skips the setFirstAndTen branch and instead advances the down using e.prePlay.down + 1 and the pre-play line to gain. Real football: possession changed twice, so the recovering team starts a fresh 1st and 10 at the recovery spot. o.turnover also stays 'int' while possessionAfter is the offense, so clockAfterPlay treats it as a turnover stop and the play is logged and counted as a turnover for a team that still has the ball.
minors.failureScenario: Team A, 1st & 10 from its own 25 (line to gain = own 35). Pass intercepted at A's own 25; the interceptor is stripped immediately and A's receiver recovers at A's own 22. applySeries: changeOfPossession false, isFirstDown(22 vs 35) false -> down 2, toGo 13. Result shown is '2nd & 13 at A 22' instead of the correct '1st & 10 at A 22'.

minors.title: Defensive two-point return credits the 2 points to the team that attempted the try
minors.description: checkCarrierBoundaries (src/sim/phases/playLive.ts:742-748) sets o.scoreKind='two', o.points=2 and emits TWO_POINT_RESULT with team = c.team whenever ANY carrier reaches his attack goal on a twoPoint play, including a defender returning an interception. applyOutcome then does addPoints(s, offense, 2) with offense = e.playOffense, i.e. the team that was attempting the conversion, so the scoreboard, stats.teams[].points and scoringByQuarter all credit the wrong team while the emitted event named the other one. The pick-six path handles this correctly (scoreKind 'td' uses o.possessionAfter, line 129), so only the conversion branch is wrong.
minors.failureScenario: Team A goes for two from the 2. A's QB is intercepted and the defender returns it to team B's attack end zone. TWO_POINT_RESULT fires with team = B (good: true), but addPoints(s, offense=A, 2) puts 2 points on A's side of the scoreboard. Note this is currently masked by the wrong-way carrier bug (finding 2) and by the 12-second safety whistle, so it will only surface once returns work.

minors.title: Third-down touchdowns count as attempts but never as conversions
minors.description: applyOutcome only sets `firstDown` from applySeries, which runs in the final `else` branch. When o.scoreKind === 'td' the function takes the touchdown branch (addPoints / nextPlayKind = 'pat') and applySeries is never called, so `firstDown` stays false. The third-down bookkeeping at line 166-168 still fires because isScrimmagePlay(o) is true and prePlay.down === 3, so recordThirdDown(s, offense, false) increments thirdDownAtt without thirdDownConv. Every third-down touchdown is recorded as a failed conversion.
minors.failureScenario: 3rd & 6 from the 12, receiver catches it for a touchdown. stats.teams[offense].thirdDownAtt += 1, thirdDownConv unchanged. Probe over 20 headless games: 25 third-down touchdowns, 0 counted as conversions — the box score reports 101/427 (23.7%) where the true figure is 126/427 (29.5%).

minors.title: Ticker names the returner (or nobody) as the kicker/punter
minors.description: describePlay fills templates 13/14 ({kicker}) and 15 ({punter}) from `carrier = this.nameOf(state, ev.carrierIdx)`. PLAY_RESULT.carrierIdx is never the kicker: for a placekick resolveFieldGoal sets spotFixed without ever assigning o.carrierIdx, so it stays null and nameOf returns the literal fallback string 'the runner'; for a punt, resolveKickReception (playLive.ts:521) sets o.carrierIdx to the *receiving team's* returner. The kicker index is available (ext.kick.kickerIdx / KICK_LAUNCHED.kickerIdx) but is not carried on the event.
minors.failureScenario: Headless game seed 4242 produces these live ticker lines verbatim: `the runner's 49-yarder is NO GOOD, wide and short.` (Q4 field goal — kicker name missing entirely) and `F. Last8 booms it 39 yards, downed at the HOM 30.` where F. Last8 is the receiving team's WR3 punt returner, not the punter (Last40). Every field goal, extra point and punt call-out in the game credits the wrong player.

minors.title: Aiming a kick also walks the kicker sideways, moving the launch point ~5 yards
minors.description: In the KICK_METER context Left/Right feed BOTH the aim accumulator (lines 108-109) and, unfiltered, the ordinary movement block at lines 118-126, which calls `stepPlayer(me, ...)` at full `maxSpeed`. The controlled player on a kick play is the K/P (playCall.ts:50-56) and `updateLiveAI` skips the controlled index, so nothing pulls him back. The meter lasts up to KICK.meterFillTicks + meterSweepTicks = 100 ticks while aimOffset saturates at KICK.aimMaxOffsetRad=0.26 after only ~65 ticks, so the remaining hold is pure lateral drift. On a punt or kickoff the kicker is also the ball carrier, so `carryBall` drags the ball with him and `launchKick` reads `from.x = p.ball.pos2.x` (playLive.ts:265-267) — the launch x moves with the drift while `spotY` stays pinned at the snap, so the ball visibly jumps back in y at release.
minors.failureScenario: Probe (GameSim, userTeam=0 kicking off, holding Right + move {x:1,y:0} through the three meter presses): the kicker walks from x=26.67 to x=31.82 (5.15 yd of drift) and the ball launches from x=32.10 instead of the 26.67 centre — a 5.4-yard lateral displacement the player never asked for. Aim hard toward one sideline on a punt and the punter is in the numbers before he strikes the ball.

minors.title: Settings advertises "H - Hard count" but PRE_SNAP_OFF has no working input except Snap
minors.description: `GameAction.HardCount` is bound to KeyH in PRE_SNAP_OFF and shown to the player on the settings key reference (SettingsScreen.ts:18, `['H', 'Hard count']`). Nothing in src/ ever reads it — grepping `GameAction.HardCount` outside Bindings/types returns nothing, and `PENALTY.offsideVsHardCount` (balance.ts:177) is likewise unreferenced, so the feature reached the bindings and the balance table but never the sim. The same holds for `GameAction.PumpFake` (Space in QB_PASSING) — bound and labelled, never read. Pre-snap directional input is also inert: `updatePreSnapAI` skips the controlled player and `preSnapPhase` never integrates anyone, and the false-start check at preSnap.ts:196-208 requires an OL to be controlled, which `chooseControlled` never does for the user (always QB/K/P on offense).

Pressing an arrow key pre-snap also does nothing (no motion, and no false start either), so there is no way to distinguish a dead key from a mistimed one.

minors.title: Field-goal "wide left/right" uses world x, so it is backwards for a team attacking -y
minors.description: `resolveFieldGoal` reports `missSide = x < CENTER_X ? 'left' : 'right'` from the raw world x of the crossing point, with no reference to `s.attackDir[e.playOffense]`. "Wide left" is a kicker-relative call: for a team attacking +y the kicker's left is world -x (correct here), but for a team attacking -y the kicker's left is world +x, so the label inverts. Since `swapEnds` flips attackDir every quarter, each team spends half the game on the wrong side of this test. The value flows straight into PlayByPlay (`this.lastFgSide = ev.missSide`, PlayByPlay.ts:202, consumed at line 357) while the user's camera is flipped to match their own attack direction (Renderer.ts:79 `cam.setOrientation(extras.viewAttackDir)`), so the commentary contradicts what the player just watched.
minors.failureScenario: User's team attacks -y in Q2 and hooks a 45-yarder so the ball crosses the plane at x = 20 (world -x, which with the flipped camera renders on the RIGHT of the screen and is the kicker's right). The event carries `missSide:'left'` and the play-by-play reads "no good, wide left" while the player watched it sail wide right.

minors.title: Hub shows an unrelated AI game as the user's matchup once the user is eliminated
minors.description: `getNextGame` falls back to `const target = userGame ?? games[0]` when the user's team has no game in the current week, then computes `opponentId`, `userIsHome` and `opponentRecord` from that stranger's game as if the user were in it. SeasonHubScreen.renderOverview (line 108) likewise falls back to `next.weekGames[0]` for the matchup card and prints "Your game is in the books — sim the rest of the week" (line 135), which is wrong — the user is eliminated, not finished. This fires for every user who misses the playoffs or loses a playoff round, i.e. at least half of all seasons (8 of 16 teams miss).

Advancing to week 15 the Overview tab reads "Next up · CONFERENCE SEMIFINALS", shows DUN @ FAI as the matchup card, and prints "You: 2-12 · Opponent: 10-4 · Away" — FAI is not ASH's opponent and ASH is not playing at all — plus the footnote claiming the user's game is in the books. Verified across 5 of 6 sampled seeds.

minors.title: Midfield logo and letter change teams at every quarter break
minors.description: fieldThemeFromTeams derives `midfieldLogo: low.logo` and `midfieldLetter: low.city[0]` from lowDefender, which is computed from attackDir[0]. End-zone assignment from attackDir is correct (teams do change ends), but the logo painted at the 50 is stadium paint and must not move. swapEnds() flips attackDir each quarter, so lowDefender alternates 0,1,0,1 across Q1-Q4 and the midfield disc repaints with the other team's logo. fieldThemeKey includes the logo params, so FieldRenderer.ensure rebuilds the whole offscreen surface with the new logo. Verified: fieldThemeFromTeams(teams, [1,-1]).midfieldLogo is the home spec ('bolt', letter 'H'); with [-1,1] it is the away spec ('star', letter 'A').
minors.failureScenario: Exhibition, Harbor (home) vs Ashford (away). Q1 shows Harbor's bolt logo at midfield. At the Q1/Q2 quarter break the camera flips and the same midfield disc now shows Ashford's star logo; it flips back for Q3 and away again for Q4.

minors.title: Replay says "ANY KEY TO SKIP" but only arrows/WASD/Enter/Esc skip
minors.description: drawReplayFrame prints the fixed hint 'ANY KEY TO SKIP'. GameSession.stepReplay (src/game/GameSession.ts:476-481) skips only when the sampled InputFrame has a non-empty `pressed` set, and InputSystem.sample resolves codes through the REPLAY binding scope, which is empty (src/input/Bindings.ts:118) and falls through to GLOBAL - arrows, WASD, Enter/NumpadEnter and Escape only. Space, Tab, digits and every other letter resolve to undefined and never produce a pressed action, so they do nothing. The binding file's own comment ("Esc/Enter skip a replay") acknowledges the narrow set the overlay text contradicts.
minors.failureScenario: A 40-yard touchdown triggers a replay that runs 240 recorded frames at 0.5x = 8 seconds of screen time. The player, who has been using Space all game for snap/dive/kick-meter, taps Space repeatedly to skip as the overlay instructs; nothing happens and they sit through the full replay.

minors.title: Kick meter drawn from the snapshot: shows for kicks the viewer cannot control
minors.description: Renderer.draw sources the overlay's kick meter from `curr.kickMeter` (the TickSnapshot) rather than from RendererExtras, and EffectsRenderer.drawOverlay draws it whenever `active` is true (line 257). preSnap.ts:123 sets kickMeter.active = true for every kick play regardless of which team is kicking or whether the kicker is user-controlled, and GameSim.snapshot publishes it unconditionally. Consequently the POWER/ACCURACY meter with its aim arrow is drawn during the opponent's punts, field goals and kickoffs, and during CPU-auto kicks by the user's own team. It is also the one overlay GameSession.replayExtras (src/game/GameSession.ts:883-902) cannot switch off - every other live overlay is nulled there, but a replay whose trimmed frame window includes the pre-launch ticks of a kick will draw the meter on top of the letterboxed replay.
minors.failureScenario: CPU punts to the user. The user, waiting in RETURN_WAIT to field the ball, sees a full-width POWER meter with a yellow aim arrow appear at the bottom of the screen, fill and lock itself, with no input of theirs having any effect on it.

minors.title: Effects list never cleared between games: old bursts replay in the next game
minors.description: App owns one Renderer (and therefore one EffectsRenderer) for the whole session and hands it to every GameSession (src/app/App.ts:102, 269). GameSession.dispose() resets zoom, audio, play-by-play and the replay buffer but never calls renderer.effects.clear() - that method has no caller outside src/render/demo.ts. Effects are timed in absolute sim ticks: EffectsRenderer.prune keeps an entry unless `tick - startTick > ttl`, and drawWorld skips it while `age < 0`. A new GameSim starts at tick 0, so any effect left over from the previous game (startTick in the thousands) is neither pruned nor drawn - until the new game's tick reaches that value, at which point it draws again at the old game's world coordinates. Up to EFFECT_STYLE.maxEffects = 48 entries can survive this way.
minors.failureScenario: Exhibition. A big hit at tick 3600 emits a 'bigHit' burst; the player hits Esc within the next 26 ticks (pause freezes stepOneTick but render/prune keeps running with the frozen tick, so the entry never ages out) and chooses Restart. About 60 seconds into the restarted game, at tick 3600, a yellow starburst pops on empty grass at the previous game's tackle spot.

minors.title: HUD shows the previous play's down, distance and spot through the PAT choice
minors.description: drawSituation suppresses the down-and-distance/BALL ON strip only for GamePhase.GAME_OVER. During POINT_AFTER_CHOICE the sim has not yet run setupPat(), so state.down/toGo/ballOnY still hold the pre-touchdown series, and the strip renders stale numbers. Overlay screens use `background: rgba(3,6,11,0.72)` (src/ui/styles.ts:53), so the strip stays legible under the PAT modal. Probe over a full headless game captured, at POINT_AFTER_CHOICE entry: Q1 "3rd & 11 · BALL ON HOM 29", Q2 "2nd & 7 · BALL ON AWY 32", Q4 "2nd & 12 · BALL ON AWY 28" - each the down and spot of the play that just scored. The related kickoff/PAT snaps show an inapplicable "1st & 10" for the same reason.
minors.failureScenario: User scores a touchdown from their own 29 on 3rd & 11. The 'Touchdown - point after' modal opens and, visible through its 72%-opaque backdrop, the scoreboard strip still reads "3rd & 11 · BALL ON HOM 29" - a down and a field position that no longer exist.

minors.title: Replay zoom invalidates the field cache, forcing two full field re-renders
minors.description: FieldRenderer.ensure keys its cached offscreen surface on `cam.pxPerYard.toFixed(3)`, and pxPerYard is derived from zoom (src/render/Camera.ts:83-88). GameSession.startReplay calls camera.setZoom(REPLAY_ZOOM=1.15) (src/game/GameSession.ts:467) and endReplay calls setZoom(1) (src/game/GameSession.ts:494), so the cache key changes at both edges of every big-play replay. Each miss allocates a fresh canvas sized up to FIELD_STYLE.maxSurfacePixels = 8,000,000 device pixels (~32MB of backing store at 1920px wide) and repaints the whole 120-yard field: 24 grass bands, two end zones with filled+stroked text, ~21 yard lines, a ~380-segment hash/tick path, 18 rotated yard numbers and the midfield logo. This is pure waste — the field content is identical, only the sampling scale changed — and it runs synchronously inside Renderer.draw on exactly the frame the highlight cuts in and the frame it cuts back out.
minors.failureScenario: Player breaks a 45-yard touchdown run. ReplayTrigger arms, startReplay sets zoom 1.15; on that frame Renderer.draw sees a new field key, allocates a ~1883x4242 canvas and repaints the entire field before drawing anything, stalling the frame. The stall repeats when the replay ends and zoom returns to 1 — a visible hitch bracketing every replay on a machine that held 60fps through the live play.

minors.title: Restart stacks a second crowd noise loop over the one still stopping
minors.description: App.beginGame calls disposeSession() first (src/app/App.ts:246), so GameSession.dispose() -> audio.stopAmbience(), which nulls graph.crowdSource but schedules the node to stop a full second later (`src.stop(now + 1.0)`). The replacement GameSession's constructor immediately calls audio.setCrowdIntensity(this.audioDirector.crowdIntensity) with CROWD.base = 0.25 (src/game/GameSession.ts:178). setCrowdIntensity clears ambienceStopped because v > 0, and applyCrowd then calls startCrowdLoop, whose only guard is `if (!g || g.crowdSource) return` — crowdSource was just nulled, so a second BufferSource is created and connected to the same crowdFilter -> crowdGain chain. Both play the same 2s brown-noise buffer at different phases into one gain node.
minors.failureScenario: Player pauses an exhibition and picks "Restart Game". App.restartGame -> beginGame disposes the old session (old loop scheduled to stop at t+1.0s) and constructs the new one, which starts a second loop at t+0. For the next second two brown-noise beds sum through crowdGain, so the crowd bed jumps roughly 3-6 dB above its set level and then abruptly drops back when the old source stops. Repeated restarts inside one second stack further sources.
